CHAPTER V
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
Part One
Prevention of Violence against Women

Article 19
Further provisions regarding the prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 16, Article 17 and Article 18 shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 18
Prevention of violence against women is carried out in an integrated and coordinated manner between those responsible for the prevention of violence against women and Regional Apparatus that oversee matters of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this regional regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Mamuju Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Mamuju Regency.
3. Bupati is the Bupati of Mamuju.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is an auxiliary element of the regional head and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region.
5. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts made by families, government and others aimed at women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights.
7. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.
8. Violence Against Women is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment, and disregards the human rights of women.
9. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to implement women's empowerment in various fields of development, as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is established by the government or community-based.
10. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the region that carry out integrated service functions for women and children victims of crime and/or violence, including as an information center for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into development.
13. Regional Action Plan for Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter referred to as RANDA PUG is a planning document as a guide in efforts to implement development strategies by integrating gender into a unified integral dimension of planning, preparation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
14. PUG Institution is an institution that meets the elements of PUG prerequisites, which functions effectively in a sustainable system with agreed norms in fulfilling the human rights of women and men fairly to achieve equality between women and men in all fields of development and levels of government.
15. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function, and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, which consists of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
16. Victim is a person who experiences violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Task force is a coordinative institution formed by the Mamuju Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Mamuju Regency.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAMUJU REGENCY
NUMBER 9 OF 2023
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Empowerment and Protection of women currently needs to receive serious attention from all parties, including attention from the Regional Government, in relation to the existence of phenomena in social and community life that often make women victims of violence and exploitation; they are often positioned as economic objects and are often excluded and/or marginalized in social interaction.

In Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (UU KDRT), it is stipulated that the state guarantees to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. Victims of domestic violence, who are mostly women and children, must receive protection in order to avoid and be free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth. Therefore, the Regional Government makes regulations related to the Empowerment and Protection of Women.

CHAPTER II
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 2
(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and Protection of Women.
(2) The efforts for Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
   a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
   b. determination of implementation guidelines;
   c. provision of services; and
   d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
(3) The efforts for Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the prevailing laws and regulations.

Second Part
Provision of Services for Women Victims of Violence

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 40
(1) The Regent implements guidance and supervision of women's empowerment and protection in the Region. (2) In implementing guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent assigns the Regional Apparatus that handles women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(3) The Regional Apparatus that handles women's empowerment and child protection affairs as referred to in paragraph (2) serves as the coordinator for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection in the Region.

Paragraph 3
Social Sector

Paragraph 2
Legal Field

CHAPTER X
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 43
Upon the entry into force of this Regional Regulation, all provisions of regional laws and regulations related to the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection that have existed thus far, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to the provisions in this Regional Regulation.

Article 44
Sufficiently Clear

1.2.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation defines “Kekerasan Terhadap Perempuan” broadly (Pasal 1 angka 8) and regulates prevention and services for women victims of violence, but it does not explicitly mention “kekerasan seksual” as a category within the operative articles. The only explicit sexual-violence reference is in the legal basis (“Undang-Undang Nomor 12 Tahun 2022 tentang Tindak Pidana Kekerasan Seksual”) in the preamble, which is a citation of higher law, not a substantive inclusion/definition of sexual violence in this local regulation. Given that, a ‘Yes’ golden label for ‘Sexual violence’ appears unsupported by the actual Indonesian text; the judge’s ‘No’ is reasonable.

1.5.translated_snippet: Empowerment and Protection of women currently needs to receive serious attention from all parties, including attention from the Regional Government, in relation to the existence of phenomena in social and community life that often make women victims of violence and exploitation; they are often positioned as economic objects and are often excluded and/or marginalized in social interaction.
1.5.evaluator_rationale: The general elucidation states that women are often positioned as economic objects and are victims of exploitation, which constitutes inclusion of economic exploitation as a relevant form of violence/abuse addressed by the regulation.

Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to implement women's empowerment in various fields of development, as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is established by the government or community-based.
10. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the region that carry out integrated service functions for women and children victims of crime and/or violence, including as an information center for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into development.

16. Victim is a person who experiences violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Task force is a coordinative institution formed by the Mamuju Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Mamuju Regency.

Article 18

Article 37

b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and children's rights; and
c. strengthening and developing institutions that provide family quality improvement services.
(2) The responsibility of Regional Governments in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by PD in accordance with their duties and functions.

Second Part

CHAPTER VI
FAMILY QUALITY
Article 31

b. strengthening and developing institutions providing family quality improvement services in realizing gender equality; and
c. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and children's rights.
(2) Efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by PD in accordance with their duties and functions.

CHAPTER IX
FUNDING
Article 42
Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women's Empowerment and Protection in the Region is sourced from:
a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. other legitimate and non-binding sources of funds.

b. provision of opportunities for women to hold public office;

d. self-development through organizations to associate, assemble and express opinions.
(2) Empowerment of women in the political field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

(6) The Regional Government and/or Political Parties are responsible for providing political education for women.

Third Part

4.2.rationale: The Indonesian regulation includes education/counseling elements tied to women’s rights and gender equality: Pasal 39(2)(a) “pemberian penyuluhan mengenai hak perempuan” and Pasal 34(c) “melakukan penyuluhan peningkatan kesetaraan gender dalam kehidupan keluarga masyarakat.” These are explicit informational/educational activities that fit ‘gender equality education’ as a primary prevention approach. Because the evidence is in the operative text and was retrieved, the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.

evidence_candidates.text:
ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAMUJU REGENCY
NUMBER 9 OF 2023
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Empowerment and Protection of women currently needs to receive serious attention from all parties, including attention from the Regional Government, in relation to the existence of phenomena in social and community life that often make women victims of violence and exploitation; they are often positioned as economic objects and are often excluded and/or marginalized in social interaction.

In Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (UU KDRT), it is stipulated that the state guarantees to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, take action against perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence. Victims of domestic violence, who are mostly women and children, must receive protection in order to avoid and be free from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth. Therefore, the Regional Government makes regulations related to the Empowerment and Protection of Women.

CHAPTER V
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
Part One
Prevention of Violence against Women

CHAPTER II
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 2
(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the empowerment and Protection of Women.
(2) The efforts for Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
   a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
   b. determination of implementation guidelines;
   c. provision of services; and
   d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
(3) The efforts for Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the prevailing laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this regional regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Mamuju Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Mamuju Regency.
3. Bupati is the Bupati of Mamuju.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is an auxiliary element of the regional head and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region.
5. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts made by families, government and others aimed at women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights.
7. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.
8. Violence Against Women is any action that violates, obstructs, eliminates enjoyment, and disregards the human rights of women.
9. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to implement women's empowerment in various fields of development, as well as the protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is established by the government or community-based.
10. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the region that carry out integrated service functions for women and children victims of crime and/or violence, including as an information center for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into development.
13. Regional Action Plan for Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter referred to as RANDA PUG is a planning document as a guide in efforts to implement development strategies by integrating gender into a unified integral dimension of planning, preparation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
14. PUG Institution is an institution that meets the elements of PUG prerequisites, which functions effectively in a sustainable system with agreed norms in fulfilling the human rights of women and men fairly to achieve equality between women and men in all fields of development and levels of government.
15. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function, and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, which consists of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
16. Victim is a person who experiences violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Task force is a coordinative institution formed by the Mamuju Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Mamuju Regency.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 40
(1) The Regent implements guidance and supervision of women's empowerment and protection in the Region. (2) In implementing guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent assigns the Regional Apparatus that handles women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(3) The Regional Apparatus that handles women's empowerment and child protection affairs as referred to in paragraph (2) serves as the coordinator for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection in the Region.

Third Part
Strengthening and Development of Institutions Providing Women's Protection Services

Article 18
Prevention of violence against women is carried out in an integrated and coordinated manner between those responsible for the prevention of violence against women and Regional Apparatus that oversee matters of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 19
Further provisions regarding the prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 16, Article 17 and Article 18 shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Second Part
Provision of Services for Women Victims of Violence

CHAPTER X
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 43
Upon the entry into force of this Regional Regulation, all provisions of regional laws and regulations related to the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection that have existed thus far, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to the provisions in this Regional Regulation.

HEAD OF MAMUJU REGENCY
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN.

6.7.rationale: Pasal 16(2) explicitly lists “perempuan dalam situasi intoleransi” as part of “kelompok perempuan rentan.” This is a targeted recognition of women vulnerable due to intolerance (commonly linked to minority status/religious/ethnic intolerance). The retrieved English passage contained this, and the judge’s interpretation is reasonable. Therefore the golden label ‘No’ appears wrong.
